strengths: Well-motivated hierarchical benchmark design that enables analysis of synergistic effects between perception, understanding, and reasoning—a feature lacking in prior work
Contemporary dataset with 53% of images from 2025 and collection from diverse international social media platforms, reducing data leakage and promoting geographic diversity
Rich multi-task annotations: each image annotated across all 8 tasks enables meaningful cross-task analysis and unified evaluation framework
Comprehensive empirical evaluation of 15+ models spanning closed-source, open-source, and reasoning-specialized variants with careful evaluation strategies
Novel statistical analysis in Section 4.4 demonstrating concrete cross-task dependencies (e.g., OC-RE correlation: 0.73) and using linear/polynomial regression to identify task predictability
Addresses underexplored area of interleaved image-text understanding through region-wise OCR tasks (>80% of benchmarks lack this per Table 1)
Rigorous data curation with two-stage quality control including duplicate detection, format checking, and privacy-aware filtering
weaknesses: Limited intellectual novelty: contribution is primarily benchmark construction and organization rather than methodological innovation or new evaluation paradigms; individual tasks (object detection, OCR, grounding, spatial reasoning) are well-established
Modest dataset scale: 3.4K images is smaller than contemporary benchmarks (MMMU: 11.5K); unclear distribution of questions across task tiers and whether this adequately represents diversity

Critical reproducibility gaps: no inter-annotator agreement (IAA) metrics reported for human annotations, annotation guidelines not provided, unclear public release timeline, and missing technical details (bounding box conversion, exact majority voting strategy)

Shallow analysis of synergistic effects: Section 4.4 demonstrates correlations but lacks explanation of *why* perception enables reasoning or provides actionable insights for model development; no error analysis or failure mode investigation
Problematic evaluation methodology: using GLM4-flash as automatic evaluator contradicts cited work (Wang et al. 2023) showing LLMs are biased evaluators; majority voting details unspecified

Incomplete bias and representativeness analysis: while low-level visual attributes are analyzed, social media selection bias, gender/demographic representation, and adequacy of 12 scenarios for real-world diversity are not addressed

No ablation studies demonstrating value of multi-level vs. single-task evaluation, no human performance baselines, and missing evidence that Lens performance correlates with downstream task generalization
Reasoning-specialized models (QVQ, Kimi-VL) underperform on reasoning tasks with no analysis of whether evaluation strategy is optimal for their chain-of-thought design

strengths: Timely contemporary dataset with 53% images from 2025 and 80%+ from September 2024, effectively addressing data leakage concerns
Well-motivated hierarchical three-tier structure (perception-understanding-reasoning) with clear articulation of synergistic effects evaluation
Comprehensive multi-level annotations allowing rich cross-task analysis with shared visual grounding across all 8 tasks
Broad evaluation coverage including 15+ frontier models released December 2024-April 2025, spanning closed and open-source systems
Interesting statistical analysis revealing moderate correlations (0.67-0.73) between lower-level and higher-order task performance
weaknesses: Critical omission: Zero inter-annotator agreement (IAA) metrics reported despite 50+ annotators and subjective tasks—this is unacceptable for a benchmark paper and prevents validation of annotation quality

Flawed reasoning task evaluation: LLM-based automatic evaluation with GLM4-flash lacks validation against human judgment and ignores documented concerns about LLM evaluators being unfair; no reported agreement with human assessment
Inconsistent evaluation methodology across tasks: perception/understanding use direct outputs while reasoning tasks use majority voting, confounding cross-task analysis and preventing fair comparison
Limited scale at 3.4K images (~7.5K questions per task) raises statistical power concerns; correlations computed on only 15 models with no significance testing or cross-validation
Limited novelty: Most tasks (OD, VG, OCR, OE, RE) are well-established; main contribution is combining existing tasks with shared images rather than developing new evaluation paradigms

Weak task analysis with minimal error analysis, no explanation for catastrophic failures (e.g., 27.24% VG), and unexplained underperformance of reasoning-specialized models despite reasoning task focus
Subjective data curation with 'complex or ambiguous images' filtered without documented criteria, introducing selection bias toward easier scenes with unquantified geographic/demographic diversity
Scene Knowledge Inference (SKI) tasks appear ad-hoc (airline selection, cafeteria pricing) without principled framework; definition of 'scene knowledge' is vague

Unvalidated claims of synergistic effects based solely on correlations (correlation ≠ causation); confounded task difficulty not disentangled (e.g., VG failures may reflect coordinate generation vs. reasoning)
Reproducibility gaps: Missing project URL, no dataset release plan, annotation guidelines not provided, evaluation prompts not detailed, no code mentioned

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark addressing genuine limitations: evaluates synergistic effects of perception on reasoning and maintains inter-task consistency through unified image annotations
Comprehensive contemporary dataset: 3.4K images with 60K+ questions, 53% from 2025, manually collected from diverse social media platforms to avoid data leakage

Unified annotation strategy: each image annotated for all 8 tasks enables powerful cross-task correlation analysis and reveals task interdependencies (OC-RE: 0.73 correlation, OCR strongly predicts reasoning)
Extensive evaluation: 15+ frontier models (closed-source, open-source, reasoning-specialized) with multiple evaluation strategies and statistical analysis of task relationships
Valuable empirical insights: identifies Visual Grounding bottleneck (even 78B models <28%), scaling trends, and that reasoning-specialized models can partially compensate for perceptual limitations
Solid technical execution: clear task definitions, reasonable metrics, documented quality control procedures, good reproducibility details
weaknesses: Critical omission: no inter-annotator agreement (IAA) metrics reported despite 50+ annotators; standard for dataset papers and essential for assessing annotation reliability, especially for subjective tasks

Privacy and ethics concerns incompletely addressed: claims copyright compliance but provides limited evidence of permissions from image creators; 53% from 2025 raises consent questions; no IRB approval mentioned

Evaluation rigor gaps: LLM-based evaluation (GLM4-flash) lacks validation against human evaluation; no inter-evaluator agreement; choice of AP₅₀ for object detection unjustified; Figure 7 regression lacks R² values and significance testing

Synergistic effects claims overstated: correlations shown but not causal relationships; no R² values reported for linear regressions; lacks experimental validation (e.g., architecture ablations) to support synergy claims
Limited error analysis: minimal qualitative examination of failure modes; identifies bottlenecks but provides few concrete examples of systematic failure patterns
Incomplete dataset bias analysis: claims to avoid regional/cultural bias with no evidence; concentration on contemporary data limits historical grounding; limited analysis of annotation biases
Missing cross-benchmark validation: no comparison of model rankings between LENS and other benchmarks (MMBench, MMMU) to validate uniqueness of insights
Reasoning task annotation details unclear: protocol for collecting detailed 'thought paths' not specified; lack of IAA particularly concerning for most subjective tasks

strengths: Well-motivated multi-level benchmark addressing genuine limitation that existing benchmarks don't assess synergistic effects between perception, understanding, and reasoning tiers
Exceptionally contemporary dataset (53% from 2025, 70% post-September 2024) with rigorous privacy protection addressing pre-training contamination concerns
Comprehensive evaluation across 15+ models with multiple evaluation strategies, human validation (97.13% agreement), and fine-grained analysis (scale-wise, resolution-dependent performance)
Strong statistical analysis revealing task dependencies through Pearson correlations (e.g., OC-OCR: 0.77), linear regression, and context-dependent synergy testing (Table 5)
SMEC framework shows consistent improvements across model scales (3-3.4% on SKI) and outperforms baselines despite modest gains
Exemplary reproducibility with detailed collection procedures, formal algorithms, meta-prompts, and ethics statement addressing privacy and copyright
Rich multi-task annotations on unified images enables controlled analysis impossible in task-specific benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited benchmark novelty—primarily advances on data contemporaneity and unified annotations rather than structural design; intuition that 'perception facilitates reasoning' is relatively unsurprising

SMEC evaluated only on SKI task and initially on 3,500-sample subset; no ablation studies clarifying which components (generation vs. screening vs. integration) drive improvements; undefined 'diversity criterion'
Synergistic effects analysis demonstrates correlation but not causation; reverse causality (general capability → both perception and reasoning) not ruled out; Table 5 uses single model on subset data
Visual grounding remains critical bottleneck (27% for InternVL3-78B, 45% for Qwen2.5-VL-72B); 0.5 IoU threshold not justified; unclear if benchmark measures reasoning or primarily VG limitations
LLM-based evaluation for open-ended tasks relies on GLM4-flash with 6.35% error on false negatives (Table 7); majority voting strategy for reasoning tasks insufficiently specified
Modest scope: 3.4K images (vs. 11.5K for MMMU), 12 scenarios with potential overlap, static images only, ~7 questions/image limit analysis depth
Model evaluation concerns: N/A entries limit comparability, reasoning models designed to avoid object detection making overall performance expected, no per-model error analysis

SMEC formalization gaps: 'diversity criterion' undefined, prompt adaptation mechanism unclear, Algorithm 1 lacks mathematical notation; limited comparison to multi-expert frameworks or test-time scaling methods
Incomplete documentation: project page link broken, unclear if dataset will be public, inter-annotator agreement unreported, annotation guidelines for subjective tasks missing
Technical issues: OC-OCR correlation (0.77) >> OC-OE (0.46) counterintuitive, only Pearson correlation reported, regression coefficients not quantitatively discussed

strengths: Well-executed and comprehensive dataset with contemporary images (53% from 2025) and careful privacy-preserving collection procedures
Rigorous statistical analysis of cross-task dependencies revealing meaningful correlations (OC-RE: 0.73, OE-OCR: 0.67) between perception and reasoning
Extensive empirical evaluation of 15+ state-of-the-art MLLMs with thorough documentation and reproducibility details
Useful qualitative error analysis identifying systematic failure modes in current models (occlusion, small objects, spatial reasoning deficits)
Transparent treatment of ethical considerations, data privacy, and human annotation practices with human-LLM agreement validation
weaknesses: SMEC framework lacks sufficient novelty—it is essentially role-based prompt engineering, a well-known technique; improvements are marginal (3-3.4% on SKI) with 3× computational cost, and only compared to Self-Refine and majority voting, missing key baselines like CoT variants and recent test-time scaling methods

Claims about 'synergistic effects' are oversold; evidence is correlational rather than causal, lacks statistical significance testing, and may simply reflect that better-performing models are good at all tasks rather than true synergistic learning

Incomplete technical specification of SMEC: 'diversity criterion' (Algorithm 1, line 8) never formally defined, redundancy filtering mechanism vague, and no ablation studies isolating component contributions

Visual Grounding task shows suspiciously poor performance across all models (27.24% for InternVL3-78B)—concerning indicator of annotation quality issues or task calibration problems that are not investigated

Dataset contribution is solid but incremental—consists of standard vision tasks (detection, counting, grounding, OCR) without novel task formulations; findings that perception enables reasoning are expected rather than surprising

Missing critical evaluations: SMEC benefits demonstrated only on SKI task, not tested on perception/understanding tasks or cross-benchmark generalization; no statistical significance testing of reported improvements; no cost-benefit analysis of 3× computational overhead

Evaluation methodology concerns: majority voting for reasoning allows models to 'gamble' toward correct answers; LLM-based evaluation while validated against humans still has unknown systematic biases; inter-annotator agreement metrics not reported for human annotations

Limited real-world impact demonstrated—all test images are static photographs (no video, documents, tables), reasoning tasks are relatively simple, and no end-to-end applications showing practical value of proposed framework

strengths: Well-executed benchmark with contemporary data (53% from 2025, >80% from Sept 2024+), reducing data contamination concerns
Thoughtful three-tier task hierarchy enabling study of capability dependencies across perception, understanding, and reasoning with unified visual contexts
Rigorous quality control with multi-stage cleaning, automated pre-screening, manual verification, and comprehensive privacy/copyright compliance
Thorough experimental evaluation of 15+ diverse MLLMs with multi-faceted analysis: correlations, resolution sensitivity, temporal generalization, and qualitative error analysis
Novel SMEC framework with adaptive expert generation and redundancy filtering, showing consistent improvements (3-4% on reasoning tasks) without external tools
Strong reproducibility foundation with detailed procedures, comprehensive appendix with prompts and algorithms, and human preference validation (97% agreement)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty—hierarchical task structures and multi-level benchmarks exist; primary contribution is incremental improvement in execution rather than fundamental innovation

Central 'synergistic effects' claims are overstated: evidence relies on correlations (not causation), synergy testing only on SKI task with modest gains (+1.56%), and no causal ablations demonstrating that low-level tasks enable high-level reasoning

SMEC evaluation scope narrow (only SKI reasoning task; generalization to perception/understanding unclear) with limited baselines (only Self-Refine + majority voting) and no computational cost analysis
Dataset scale modest for a 'comprehensive' benchmark (3.4K images across 8 tasks/12 scenarios; ~7.5 questions per image) without demonstrated advantage over MMBench or similar scales

Evaluation methodology concerns: GLM4-flash as evaluator creates potential LLM-friendly bias; human preference validation limited (10 annotators, ~200 samples); majority voting for reasoning suboptimal

Incomplete synergy analysis: regression uses all models jointly (may not hold within individual models), OC-OCR correlation unexpectedly high and explained post-hoc, no investigation of architecture-dependent synergies
Error analysis lacks systematic categorization—failure modes illustrated but not quantified; claims about spatial/physical deficits not rigorously analyzed
Missing details: Project page URL incomplete, dataset availability for reproduction not stated, computational requirements not discussed, inter-annotator agreement not reported
